panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: 8-day-old female with MSUD, panel A DWI/ADC pair at cerebellar level showing symmetric restricted diffusion consistent with cerebellar MSUD edema. B: MSUD neonate, panel B DWI/ADC pair at pontine brainstem level showing brainstem restricted diffusion. C: MSUD neonate, panel C DWI/ADC pair at midbrain-thalamic level showing brainstem restricted diffusion; thalamic involvement also described but not in vocabulary. D: MSUD neonate, panel D DWI/ADC pair at basal ganglia level showing symmetric pallidal involvement. E: MSUD neonate, panel E DWI/ADC pair at internal capsule / basal ganglia level showing restricted diffusion. F: MSUD neonate, panel F DWI/ADC pair at corona radiata / pre-postcentral level showing corticospinal tract restricted diffusion corresponding to precentral/postcentral involvement.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is FLAIR brain MRI in MSUD case showing dorsal brainstem and cerebellar edema as captioned, characteristic symmetric MSUD pattern. B: Panel B is diffusion-weighted MRI showing bright dorsal midbrain and cerebellar white matter restriction as captioned for MSUD. C: Panel C is FLAIR MRI showing posterior fossa hyperintensity in medulla/vermis/cerebellar region as captioned for MSUD. D: Panel D is diffusion MRI showing marked cerebellar white matter and dorsal brainstem restriction as captioned for MSUD.

panels.body_site: brain: pons, vermis, cerebellum, optic chiasma
panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is FLAIR MRI of MSUD patient showing symmetric hyperintense edema signals in pons and cerebellum/vermis as stated in caption; mapped to dorsal brainstem and cerebellar edema vocabulary terms. B: Panel B is diffusion MRI of MSUD patient with explicit caption stating diffusion restriction in pons and cerebellum/vermis, classic symmetric MSUD edema pattern.
panels.attribution_text: K K et al. Maple Syrup Urine Disease: An Uncommon Cause of Neonatal Febrile Seizures.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.40826. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Subtle FLAIR hyperintense are signals noted in the optic chiasma, pons, vermis, and cerebellum. Mild subdural collection is noted in the bilateral cerebellar hemisphere (A). Diffusion restriction is noted in the optic chiasma, pons, vermis, and cerebellum (B). FLAIR: fluid-attenuated inversion recovery
